variables.meaning: the angle of incidence, measured from the perpendicular to the surface at the point where the ray strikes it
the angle of reflection, measured from the same perpendicular, which equals the angle of incidence
the speed of light in a vacuum, a fixed value and one of the basic physical quantities
the observed speed of light in a material, which is always less than its speed in a vacuum
the index of refraction of a material, the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in the material
the index of refraction of the medium the ray starts in
the index of refraction of the medium the ray crosses into
the angle between the incident ray and the perpendicular to the surface, in medium 1
the angle between the refracted ray and the perpendicular to the surface, in medium 2
the critical angle, the angle of incidence that produces an angle of refraction of 90°
the angle of incidence inside the denser medium, which is compared with the critical angle
the angle of refraction in the second medium, which reaches 90° at the critical angle
the index of refraction of the medium the ray travels in, which must be the larger of the two
the index of refraction of the medium beyond the surface, which must be the smaller of the two
the wavelength of the light, which decides both the color the eye sees and the index of refraction the medium presents
the index of refraction of a medium at one wavelength, which grows as the wavelength falls
the focal length of the lens, the distance from its center to its focal point, positive for a converging lens and negative for a diverging one
the power of the lens, the inverse of its focal length in meters
the object distance, the distance of the object from the center of the lens
the image distance, the distance of the image from the center of the lens, positive for a real image and negative for a virtual one
the height of the object
the height of the image, positive where the image is upright and negative where it is inverted
the magnification, the ratio of image height to object height
the radius of curvature of a spherical mirror, twice its focal length
the focal length of the mirror, positive for a concave converging mirror and negative for a convex diverging one
the power of the mirror, the inverse of its focal length in meters
the object distance, the distance of the object from the center of the mirror
the image distance, positive for a real image in front of the mirror and negative for a virtual image behind it
the height of the object
the height of the image, negative where the image is inverted
the magnification, the ratio of image height to object height
